newsitem.headline: FULL UK TEXT - BT and MCI to merge.

text.p: BRITISH TELECOMMUNICATIONS PUBLIC LIMITED COMPANY
4th November 1996
BRITISH TELECOMMUNICATIONS PLC ("BT") TO MERGE WITH MCI COMMUNICATIONS CORPORATION ("MCI")
Move creates Premier global telecoms company
BT and MCI today announced that they have entered into a merger agreement to create a premier global company well positioned to take advantage of the rapidly evolving telecommunications industry.

The merger combines the substantial financial resources and global position of BT with the growth momentum and market expertise of MCI, known for its success in the competitive US long distance market.
BT first acquired its 20 per cent. holding in MCI in 1994 when the two companies also established the highly successful Concert Communications Services joint venture.

This joint venture has been developed by the management of BT and MCI together into a leading provider of global services and solutions to 3,000 multi-national companies with over $1.5 billion in revenue under contract.
The new company will be called Concert plc ("Concert").
The company, incorporated in the UK, will have headquarters in London and Washington DC.
Concert will operate under the BT and MCI brand names in the UK and USA respectively.

The Merger will create a world leading communications power house with annual revenues of over 25 billion ($42 billion), annual cash flow from operations of about 7.5 billion ($12.3 billion), and 43 million business and residential customers in 70 countries.
At close of business last Thursday (the day before the speculation concerning the Merger) the market capitalisation of BT was 22.6 billion and the market capitalisation of MCI was $17.2 billion.
The share price of MCI at close of business last Thursday was $25.125.

Concert will provide its customers with the full range of communications services, including local, long distance, international, mobile, multi-media, Internet-based services and systems integration for business customers.
Sir Iain Vallance, Chairman of BT, said: "Concert will be exceptionally well placed to play a leading role in the major growth areas of the changing global communications market place.

"The complementary strengths and skills of BT and MCI will enable Concert to take full advantage of the great opportunities provided by the forthcoming liberalisation of telecommunications markets in the US and Europe.
"We believe this merger will provide major benefits for the shareholders, customers and employees of both BT and MCI."

Bert Roberts, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of MCI, said: "This merger creates the premier telecommunications company of the new millennium. Financial muscle, global customers and brands and customer-driven innovation will provide a strong competitive advantage as we open up communications markets both domestically and around the world.
Concert's scale will allow it to pursue major opportunities in new markets while maintaining the financial stability that comes from strong core businesses in the developed markets of the US and UK."
The combination of BT and MCI will:
* create a telecommunications group with significant
global reach;
* create one of the largest integrated international

providers of end-to-end telecommunications services with the ability to meet the global needs of multi-national companies and to compete effectively in the rapidly liberalising worldwide telecommunications market;
* combine the different management skills, background and
experience within BT and MCI in fixed line, wireless and multi-media technologies allowing the new group to capitalise and build on the diverse expertise in each company.

Immediate opportunities will be created for significant revenue enhancements and material savings in operating costs and capital expenditure. Based on a joint preliminary evaluation, the Boards of the two companies are targeting pre-tax synergy benefits arising from a full integration of the two businesses at approximately 1.5 billion ($2.5 billion) cumulatively over five years following the closing of the Merger.
Annual pre-tax synergy benefits are estimated at 500 million ($825 million) by the fifth year following the Merger.
MCI US Business

The merger with MCI will give BT's shareholders a full and direct exposure to the United States, the world's largest and most dynamic marketplace where 40 per cent. of the world's largest multi-national companies are headquartered.

MCI's core business is the provision of domestic and international long-distance telecommunications in the United States, accounting for more than 90 per cent. of MCI's operating revenues and operating income during each of the last three financial years.
The business has been growing rapidly and over the last four financial years revenues grew by an average of 12.6 per cent. p.a. and earnings per share by 11.6 per cent. p.a.
The passing of the US Telecommunications Act 1996 is expected to open the US market to full competition.

In particular, it should enable MCI to compete in the US local market from which it has been largely excluded to date. This market is immense, with total revenues in 1995 of nearly $100 billion, and profitable (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation in 1995 of $43 billion).

By combining with BT, MCI will gain access to BT's technical expertise in the provision of local market products and services. In addition, the financial strength of the combined group will enable an aggressive move into this market at the earliest available opportunity.

With customer surveys supporting the desire for "one stop shopping", MCI believes that customers are very likely to award MCI their local telecommunications business in conjunction with embedded MCI services.

In its core business, MCI derives two thirds of its revenue from business customers. Increasingly, these customers have come to rely on MCI for sophisticated, value added services. MCI believes that the combination of MCI's strong customer relationships and its robust portfolio of integrated services will be difficult for the Regional Bell Operating Companies to replicate.
Board and Management
Concert will be managed by current BT and MCI executives.

Sir Iain Vallance, the Chairman of BT, and Bert Roberts, the Chairman of MCI,will be appointed Co-Chairmen of Concert. Sir Peter Bonfield, the Chief Executive of BT, will become Chief Executive of Concert.
Gerald H Taylor, the President and Chief Operating Officer of MCI will become President and Chief Operating Officer of Concert, reporting to Sir Peter Bonfield.
Sir Peter Bonfield and Gerald H Taylor will comprise the Office of the Chief Executive to which the senior management team will report.
Robert Brace, Group Finance Director of BT, and Doug Maine, CFO of MCI, will join these four as executive members of the Board of Concert.

Sir Colin Marshall, non-executive Deputy Chairman of BT, will become non-executive Deputy Chairman of Concert, and there will be eight other non-executive Directors, to be drawn equally from the Boards of the two companies.
Merger Terms and Implementation

Under the terms of the Merger, at closing MCI shareholders (other than BT) will be entitled to receive, for each MCI share held, 0.54 new Concert American Depository Shares ("ADSs") (being the same as 0.54 BT ADSs representing 10 ordinary shares in BT) and a cash payment of $6.00. Based on the fully diluted number of MCI shares the cash payment will total up to $3.8 billion (2.3 billion).
Following the Merger, MCI shareholders will own around 34 per cent of the fully diluted share capital of the enlarged group.

The Merger is subject to a number of material conditions including regulatory, tax and other consents and confirmations in the UK, the US and Europe and the approval of BT's and MCI's shareholders. The Merger is expected to be completed by Autumn 1997.
Special Dividend
The Board of BT believes that shareholder value and earnings growth will be enhanced through the introduction of more gearing.

Accordingly, the Board of BT has decided to pay a special dividend of 35p per share (net) to BT shareholders. The special dividend is expected to be paid at the same time as the final dividend for the year ending March 31, 1997 (to be paid in September 1997). The special dividend is not conditional upon the Merger proceeding and will not be followed by a share consolidation.
Share Buy-back

Following closing of the Merger, Concert will favourably consider, subject to shareholder approval, making repurchases of its own shares. Powers to purchase up to 10 per cent. of the enlarged share capital will be sought at the Extraordinary General Meeting of BT to be held to approve the Merger.
Financial Effects

The enlarged group will be financially powerful, with combined cash flow from operations of over 7.5 billion ($12.3 billion). The gearing (net debt to equity) of the Group after the Merger and the special dividend is expected to be around 65 per cent.

The enlarged group will be able to maintain substantial capital expenditure inexisting operations as well as investing for growth in new markets, while continuing a competitive dividend policy, being able to buy back shares and reducing gearing over time.

The addition of MCI profits and the incremental profits arising from extra revenues and reduced costs are anticipated to generate earnings growth at Concert comfortably superior to that which BT could achieve on its own. For BT shareholders, the Merger is expected to lead to modest earnings dilution in the year ending March 31, 1998.
Dividend Policy

The Board of BT is forecasting dividends of 19.85p per share (net) for the year ended March 31, 1997 (excluding the special dividend), an increase of 6.1 per cent over the corresponding period last year. Dividends will continue to be an important component of shareholder value. BT's dividend policy is not going to be affected by the Merger. BT's Board believes that its earnings and cash flow will continue to be strong enough to support a growing dividend (as adjusted for the effect of the special dividend). The intention will be to grow earnings at a higher level, which would lead to an increase in dividend cover over time.
BT Half Year Results to September 30, 1996

BT's results for the half year and second quarter to September 30, 1996 will be released on November 14, 1996. The Board of BT has declared an interim dividend of 7.90 pence (net) per ordinary share payable in February. This dividend will represent a 6.0 per cent. increase on last year's interim dividend. Accordingly, the final dividend will be 11.95 pence (net) per ordinary share.
For ease of reference, in this document, all currency conversions between pounds sterling and US dollars have been made at a rate of $1.64 : 1.

DETAILS OF MERGER
1. Introduction

The Boards of British Telecommunications plc ("BT") and MCI Communications Corporation ("MCI") announce that they have entered into a Merger Agreement providing for the merger of the two groups ("the Merger"). BT first acquired its 20 per cent. holding in MCI in 1994 when the two companies also established the highly successful Concert joint venture. BT will be renamed Concert plc ("Concert"). Under the terms of the Merger: * MCI shareholders (other than BT) will be entitled to
receive at
closing for each MCI share held 0.54 new Concert American
Depository Shares ("ADSs") (being the same as 0.54 BT ADSs
representing 10 ordinary shares in BT) and a cash payment of
$6.00. * following the Merger, BT shareholders will hold approximately 66 per cent. and MCI shareholders approximately 34 per cent. of the fully diluted share capital of the enlarged group.

The Merger will be effected pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger under Delaware law and is conditional upon, amongst other things, shareholder approvals and a number of regulatory, tax and other consents and confirmations in the UK, the US and Europe.

BT's lead financial advisers are N M Rothschild & Sons Limited and Rothschild Inc. (together "Rothschilds"). Morgan Stanley & Co. Limited ("Morgan Stanley") are acting jointly as financial advisers to BT. MCI is being advised by Lazard Freres & Co. LLC and Lazard Brothers & Co., Limited (together "Lazards"). Cazenove & Co. are acting as stockbrokers to BT.
2. Background to and Reasons for the Merger

The market for voice and data services worldwide is undergoing substantial structural change. Evolving and newly developed technology, emerging increased competition in increasingly liberalised markets and the desire of customers to have most or all of their various communication needs fulfilled by one supplier, are causing suppliers, including BT and MCI, to offer, either directly or through alliances with others, new services in their own but more particularly across international markets.

In 1994, BT and MCI formed a major strategic alliance, Concert Communications Services, which has focused on providing network-based services to multinational and major national businesses primarily in Europe and North America. Concert Communications Services has achieved a market leading position in the provision of international enhanced voice and data services,with over 3,000 customers.Concert Communications Services has over $1.5 billion revenue under contract.
This alliance has formed a major part of each company's international strategy. At the time of the creation of Concert Communications Services, BT acquired a 20 per cent. stake in MCI.

Both companies have worked well together for the past two years in developing Concert Communications Services. This alliance has pooled the technical and marketing resources of both companies and has achieved a successful track record of consistent and innovative service to customers. From this foundation and as a response to the continuing liberalisation of the markets for voice and data services, both companies believe it is a natural progression to merge.

The proposed transaction will join together two strong companies with a shared vision of global excellence and leadership. The enlarged group will have significant strength and depth with the ability to provide end-to-end services across the world and the capability of meeting the challenges of the rapidly evolving international market for voice and data services. 3. Benefits of the Merger
Growth Prospects
* The new group will address some of the world's biggest and
fastest growing markets, including:
- the US business customer market
- the US local exchange market
- the liberalising European telecoms world

* The group will be even more attractive to potential international partners and to shareholders than either BT or MCI independently. * The group will have the financial resources to enable it to continue to invest in its networks whilst pursuing other opportunities to pursue growth organically, and through acquisitions and joint ventures.
Global Reach
The combination of BT and MCI will:
* create a global telecommunications group with a significant
presence in two of the world's largest telecommunications
markets (USA and Europe).
* capitalise on shared ambitions, skills and resources to develop
activities in key markets including the Asia Pacific Region.
* create one of the largest integrated international providers of
end-to-end telecommunications services with the ability to
compete effectively in the rapidly liberalising worldwide
telecommunications market.
* create a group which can provide seamless telecommunications
services to multi-national companies worldwide by serving
all product markets including local, long distance and
international, mobile, multimedia and Internet services and
network-based 'solutions' for business customers.
* create through the merger of Syntegra and MCI Systemhouse a
global systems integration business of appropriate scale and
geographic spread with the ability to meet customers' needs
across a range of applications and to become the partner of
choice for specialist consulting and computer companies.
Full and direct presence in the US
* Following the Merger the group will have approximately 45 per cent. of its revenues in North America.
* In addition, as a consequence of the Merger the enlarged group will have a significant base of shareholders in the US. Strong Management Teams
* The Merger will combine the different management skills,
background and experience within BT and MCI in fixed line,
wireless and multi-media technologies, allowing the new
group to capitalise on the diverse expertise in each
company.
* BT's experience in providing local telecoms services to
customers will be invaluable to MCI as it enters the US
local market.
* MCI's expertise and proven success in the opening of new
markets to competition will greatly enhance the group's
ability to win market share as telecommunications services
are liberalised worldwide particularly building on the
established BT position in Continental Europe.
Additional Revenues and Reduced Costs
* Immediate opportunities will be created for significant
revenue enhancements and material savings in operating
costs and capital expenditure. Based on a joint
preliminary evaluation, the Boards of the two companies are
targeting pre-tax synergy benefits arising from a full
integration of the two businesses at approximately 1.5
billion ($2.5 billion) cumulatively over five years
following the closing of the Merger. Annual pre-tax
synergy benefits are estimated at 500 million ($825
million) by the fifth year following the Merger.
Benefits include:
- software development, associated with the use of
common platforms infrastructure and services
- global purchasing and operating efficiencies. These
will
include volume discounts on world-wide purchases of
administrative assets, and combining complementary
businesses, facilities and personnel
- revenue enhancements, in particular from an integrated
management team and improved global marketing
- lower depreciation expense, from a $1.5 billion
reduction
in capital expenditure cumulatively over five years,
resulting from enhanced network utilisation and
configuration, use of common platforms, and equipment
purchasing efficiencies.
* No significant capital expenditure is expected to be required to realise these savings given the limited overlap between the businesses, although some one-time restructuring costs will be incurred.
4. Merged Group Board and Headquarters
Concert will be managed by current BT and MCI executives.

Sir Iain Vallance, the Chairman of BT, and Bert Roberts, the Chairman of MCI, will be appointed Co-Chairmen of Concert. Sir Peter Bonfield, the Chief Executive of BT, will become Chief Executive of Concert.

Gerald H Taylor, the President and Chief Operating Officer of MCI will become President and Chief Operating Officer of Concert reporting to Sir Peter Bonfield. Sir Peter Bonfield and Gerald H Taylor will comprise the Office of the Chief Executive, to which the senior management team will report.
Robert Brace, Group Finance Director of BT, and Doug Maine, CFO of MCI, will join these four as executive members of the Board of Concert.

Sir Colin Marshall, non-executive Deputy Chairman of BT, will become non-executive Deputy Chairman of Concert, and there will be eight other non-executive Directors, drawn equally from the Boards of the two companies.

In the period to closing, Bert Roberts, on behalf of the boards of directors of MCI and BT, will assume management and oversight of the integration planning of the two companies' international and correspondent activities (including Concert Communications Services) to the extent permissible under antitrust and regulatory laws.
In addition, Gerald H Taylor is now joining the BT Board. Sir Colin Marshall and Keith Oates will be joining the MCI Board.
Concert, incorporated in the UK, will have headquarters in London and Washington DC.
5. Organisational Structure
The enlarged group will organise along geographic and customer lines.

Each company will continue to sell business and consumer services under their own brand names in their respective home markets through separate operations. In addition, several new divisions will be formed from the current operations of the two companies including a global systems integration division, an international correspondent relations division, a division responsible for multi-media and a division responsible for global alliances and joint ventures.
The enlarged group expects to be able to speed up product development, create new and more efficient distribution channels and improve materially customer services.
The senior management team of the new company will be as set out in Appendix I.
6. Revenues and Earnings

MCI was founded in 1968 and has shown dramatic growth to achieve a 20 per cent. market share in the United States, capturing over 40 per cent. of the growth in the US long distance market over the last five years. In recent years, MCI has achieved faster growth in revenues and earnings (before exceptional items) than BT.
Further information on MCI is set out in Appendix IV.
Market forecasts for the US telecommunications market and for MCI in particular continue to predict growth in revenues and earnings in excess of market forecasts for BT.

The addition of MCI profits and the incremental profits arising from extra revenues and reduced costs are anticipated to generate earnings growth at Concert comfortably superior to that which BT is currently expected to achieve on its own.
For BT shareholders the Merger is expected to lead to modest earnings dilution in the year ending March 31, 1998.

The proposed strategy of MCI to enter the US local market following the introduction of the US Telecommunications Act 1996 presents significant long term opportunities for MCI, although it could require heavy initial capital investment leading to operating losses in the early years.
7. Capital Structure and Gearing

BT has reviewed its cash requirements both on a standalone basis and in the context of the enlarged group. At March 31, 1996, BT had net debt of 948 million. The Board believes that Concert will have strong cashflows from operations to meet capital expenditure requirements and to service a growing dividend for the enlarged group.
BT believes that it is in the interests of shareholder value to introduce greater gearing into the group's balance sheet.
This will be achieved in the following ways:
Cash Component of Merger Consideration
The merger consideration includes a cash amount of up to 2.3 billion ($3.8 billion), based on the fully diluted number of MCI shares.
Special Dividend

It has also been decided that it would be appropriate to return cash to the existing BT shareholders amounting to 2.2 billion. This will be done through a special dividend of 35p per share (net), further details of which are set out in section 8 below.
Future Share Buybacks

Concert will also consider favourably making re-purchases of its own shares following closing of the Merger and in ensuing years. Power to purchase up to 10 per cent of the enlarged group's share capital will be sought at the extraordinary general meeting of BT ("EGM") to be held to approve the Merger and is expected to be renewed annually at the 1998 AGM and thereafter.

If market conditions are appropriate, and subject to shareholder approval, Concert will favourably consider purchasing shares following closing of the Merger. Decisions on the amount of cash to be used in buying back shares and the precise timing will depend in part on market conditions at the time and other opportunities that exist for the deployment of Concert's resources.

The legislation announced on October 8, 1996 (see below) will, if enacted, apply to any such share buy-back. Accordingly, although Concert will remain liable to account for advance corporation tax in respect of the income element of any share buy-back, the main effect of the legislation will be that Concert shareholders will not be able to reclaim in cash any part of the tax credit attaching to that income element.
Effect on Gearing (net debt to equity)

Taking into account the special dividend and the cash consideration, BT estimates that the balance sheet at closing would have gearing of approximately 65 per cent. BT believes that gearing may rise slightly from this level in the short term as capital is committed to Concert's expansion plans in Europe and the US local market but that this will begin to fall after 1998. Interest cover will be very comfortable. Concert's cashflow is expected to remain strong and to be more than adequate to cover its capital commitments and the dividend payments on the enlarged capital, as well as to fund share repurchases.
8. Special Dividend
It is expected that the special dividend of 35p per share (net) will be paid at the same time as the final dividend for the year ending March 31, 1997 (to be paid in September, 1997).
The special dividend is not conditional upon the Merger proceeding and will not be followed by a consolidation of BT's shares.

In a Press Release dated October 8, 1996 the UK Government announced that legislation would be introduced in the Finance Bill 1997 affecting the tax treatment of share buy-backs and certain dividends.

The legislation, if enacted, will apply to share buy-backs made and dividends affected paid after October 7, 1996. The effect of the legislation, broadly, will be to deny any repayable tax credit in respect of share buy-backs or certain dividends. It is not expected that this legislation will apply to the special dividend. The position will, however, become clearer when draft legislation is published in January 1997.
Subject to the potential application of this legislation, certain BT ordinary shareholders may be able to reclaim a tax credit relating to the special dividend.

Application for clearance under Section 707 of the Income and Corporation Taxes Act 1998 will be made. It is anticipated that any such clearance will not extend to shareholdings acquired after November 1, 1996, the last day of dealings prior to this announcement.
9. Dividend Forecast and Future Policy

The Board of BT is forecasting dividends per share of 19.85p (net) for the year ending March 31, 1997 (excluding the special dividend), an increase of 6.1 per cent. over the corresponding period last year.

The Board intends to adjust the base level of the total annual dividends to a level which reflects the special dividend. This adjustment will first be made for the interim dividend for the year ending March 31, 1998. If this adjustment had been made to the total dividends for year ended March 31, 1996 of 18.7p per share, the dividend for that year would have been 16.8p per share.
Dividends will continue to be an important component of shareholder value.

BT's dividend policy is not going to be affected by the Merger. BT's Board believe that its earnings and cash flow will continue to be strong enough to support a growing dividend (as adjusted for the effect of the special dividend).
The intention will be to grow earnings at a higher level, which would lead to an increase in dividend cover over time.
10. Structure of the Transaction
Structure

The new company will be called Concert plc. Its shares will remain listed in London and Japan and its ADSs in the US. The Merger will be effected in accordance with the terms of an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated November 3, 1996 (the "Merger Agreement") entered into between BT, a wholly owned US subsidiary of BT and MCI.
It is intended to form a new subsidiary of BT with BT's existing name to run BT's existing UK core business, subject to regulatory and tax considerations.
A brief description of the Merger Agreement and the conditions to the implementation of the Merger are set out in Appendix II.
Merger Terms
Under the terms of the Merger, MCI shareholders (other than BT) will receive:
For every share of 0.54 Concert ADSs
common stock of MCI (being the same as 0.54
("MCI Common Stock") BT ADSs representing 10
ordinary shares in BT)
and $6.00 in cash
and so in proportion for any other amount of MCI Common Stock.

MCI stockholders will not receive BT dividends in respect of the year ending March 31, 1997 nor the special dividend (which is expected to be paid to BT Shareholders as part of the final dividend for that year) irrespective of the date of closing of the Merger. As long as the merger closes before March 31, 1998, MCI shareholders will receive in full the BT dividend for the year ending March 31, 1998.
Shareholder Approvals and Other Conditions
(a) BT

The Merger will be subject to the approval by 75 per cent. of those BT shareholders present and voting at the EGM. BT shareholders will also be asked to approve, amongst other things, a general authority to buy back shares, a change of name of the company and changes to the company's Articles of Association to reflect the Merger terms.
The Merger Agreement is conditional upon such approvals being obtained and the satisfaction or waiver of the other conditions in the Merger Agreement.

The formal documentation relating to the Merger will be despatched to BT shareholders as soon as practicable. This documentation will include the notice of EGM of BT shareholders, full details of the Merger and a prospectus relating to BT and will specify the necessary actions to be taken by BT shareholders.
(b) MCI

The Merger is conditional upon, amongst other matters, the adoption of the Merger Agreement by the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of MCI's common stock and the satisfaction or waiver of the other conditions in the Merger Agreement.
The Merger will become effective at the time of the filing of a certificate ofmerger with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, wh
ich is expected to be in Autumn 1997.

In order to effect the issue and the listing in the US of the new Concert ADSs to be issued pursuant to the Merger, a registration statement on Form F-4, which will include a combined proxy statement/prospectus for the MCI stockholders, will be filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") as soon as practicable.

Following the Form F-4 being declared effective by the SEC, the proxy statement/prospectus will be despatched to MCI stockholders. The proxy statement/prospectus will contain a notice convening a special meeting of MCI stockholders, to be held following the despatch of the proxy statement/prospectus, at which MCI shareholders (including BT) will be asked to adopt the Merger Agreement.
Consent and Timing
Application will be made to the relevant UK, US and European authorities for the appropriate consents and clearances.
The Merger is conditional on these approvals and the approvals of the BT and MCI shareholders. Due to the need for regulatory approvals, the Merger is expected to be completed in Autumn 1997.
11. Settlement, Listing and Dealing

BT will be seeking a US listing for the new Concert ADSs to be issued to MCI stockholders. Application will also be made to the London Stock Exchange for the new Concert ordinary shares underlying these ADSs to be admitted to the Official List.
Further details on settlement, listing and dealing will be included in the documents to be sent to BT and MCI shareholders. 12. Recommendation

The Board of BT (other than Bert Roberts, who is a Director of MCI), which has been so advised by its financial advisors N M Rothschild & Sons Limited, Rothschild Inc. and Morgan Stanley & Co. Limited, considers the terms of the Merger to be fair and reasonable to BT shareholders as a whole.

In giving their advice, Rothschilds and Morgan Stanley have relied upon the BT Board's views of the commercial merits of the Merger. The Board of BT (other than Bert Roberts) intends unanimously to recommend its shareholders to vote in favour of the resolutions to be proposed at the EGM, as they intend to do in respect of their respective beneficial holdings.

The Board of MCI (other than Sir Peter Bonfield and Dr Alan Rudge who are Directors of BT and Alfred Mockett who is an employee of BT) has unanimously recommended its shareholders to vote in favour of the resolutions to be proposed at the shareholder meeting of MCI. The Board of MCI is being advised by Lazards.
13. Other
This announcement does not constitute an offer or invitation to purchase any securities.
For ease of reference, in this document all currency conversions between pounds sterling and US dollars have been made at a rate of $1.64 : 1.
